gaps.sentence: ___ most people agree that change is needed.
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' in a general sense takes no article.

gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

gaps.sentence: He earns fifty thousand pounds ___ year.
gaps.explanation: 'Fifty thousand a year' — 'a' = per in rates.

gaps.sentence: We visited ___ Louvre on our last morning in Paris.
gaps.explanation: Most famous buildings and monuments take 'the': the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower.

gaps.sentence: I only need ___ few more minutes to finish.
gaps.explanation: 'A few minutes' = some minutes; 'few' alone would mean almost none.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He considers himself ___ expert on medieval art.
gaps.explanation: 'An expert' — 'expert' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.
